source.title: KuroNet: Regularized Residual U-Nets for End-to-End Kuzushiji Character Recognition
source.authors: Alex Lamb; Tarin Clanuwat; A. Kitamoto

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports held-out recognition results for regularization and model-capacity ablations, but it does not measure training error or directly test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior optimizer-generalization findings to motivate SGD, but reports no Adam-versus-SGD result of its own. Its own ablations test random cropping and other added regularization, plus a smaller U-Net; these results concern held-out performance but do not directly test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The authors use prior optimizer-generalization findings to justify momentum SGD, but report no controlled optimizer comparison. Their own results compare recognition systems and a bundled regularization recipe; none measures V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: updated KuroNet improves overall recognition, with three book-level F1 decreases and remaining difficulties involving rare characters, extreme character sizes, and annotations. The authors also identify broader document coverage and reading-order text output as future challenges.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Kuzushiji page recognition with a residual U-Net and multiple regularizers; it does not use the random-label, width-sweep, optimizer-comparison, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example protocols in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Added regularization slightly lowers F1 on books 200008003, 200008316, and 200010454; the paper also reports that higher test resolution can produce more false positives from unlabeled annotations.

fits_no_version.finding: Improved regularization raises reported overall precision from 0.7964 to 0.8889, recall from 0.7509 to 0.9025, and F1 from 0.7730 to 0.8957. F1 decreases slightly on three books.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The updated KuroNet recipe improves overall held-out Kuzushiji recognition, with variation across books.

fits_no_version.finding: UNet-Small has F1 0.4943 versus KuroNet's 0.7730, but both use convolutional architectures and differ in residual structure and character vocabulary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KuroNet outperforms the standard U-Net comparator restricted to 400 common characters in this recognition setup.

record.problems: The study reports held-out recognition metrics, not training error or a train-test gap, and does not isolate the contribution of each added regularizer in the aggregate comparison. Performance is aggregated across 15 books, with book-level variation including three lower F1 results under added regularization. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 contains per-book F1 values for three model variants, and Tables 4–5 contain per-book precision and recall. Those additional book-by-book values are not extracted; the aggregate Table 2 results and the text-stated three-book reversal are retained.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep, zero-training-error threshold, or widening beyond interpolation.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison or isolation of local connectivity.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning-budget comparison. The earlier conference system used Adam, but several other changes accompany the switch.
No batch-size comparison; the reported training uses batch size one.
No dropout experiment or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gap, or comparison of generalization measures.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out recognition improvements alone do not test these specific generalization claims. The decisive issue is the absence of the named comparisons, rather than missing training error alone. Per-book results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep or test-error results around or beyond the interpolation threshold.
No fully connected image classifier comparison or test isolating local connectivity.
No optimizer comparison; SGD is used, and the Adam comparison is cited prior work.
Only batch size one is reported; no batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch test.
No dropout experiment or joint dropout and weight-decay removal experiment.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining experiment.
